correctness.rationale: Exact commutator identity follows by the affine group law. For fixed unit valuations i,j, the translation-variable map has image ideal of depth min(m,(k-1)i+min(i,j)) and each point has q^(m+rho) preimages. The shell counts cover all units. Fixed-right-argument Engelizers are crossed-homomorphism kernels and their orders follow by solving a principal-ideal congruence, including the cases v=1 and k=1. Sharp stabilization was proved separately at q=2 and q>2. A dependency-free enumerator, independently multiplying group elements, checked all word targets and fixed-argument kernel sizes in 16 finite cases, up to 250000 pairs in one case; the general proof does not rely on extrapolation.

value.rationale: For an unbounded, naturally defined finite group family, the Engel word is a canonical multiplication invariant. The complete prescribed-value laws, subgroup-size multiplicities and exact transition from nilpotence to stationary nontrivial word outputs identify substantive behavior not contained in knowing first commuting probability. Nonisomorphic chain-ring affine groups share the entire invariant; that precise blindness is itself informative. The result is not merely a one-parameter special case or a small census.
